findings.claim: The repair's assertion that the fresh entityfix-tagged regate lines are the LAST records for this unit in verdicts-vfinal/ holds in four of the five files but not in verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl, which was never refreshed and carries no entityfix record at all.
findings.evidence: pipeline/synthetic/batches/batch8/verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gkey-resolved.jsonl: the last elf-b8-002 records are lines 26-30, executed_by 'claude-opus-4-8/G-KEY' (vote 2), i.e. pre-rename. Grep for 'entityfix' across batch8 returns hits only in verdicts-gdistractor.jsonl (21-25), verdicts-gkey-1.jsonl (21-25), verdicts-gkey-2.jsonl (21-25) and verdicts-gstem.jsonl (10-14). Sibling repair batch14/las-b14-001 left its gkey-resolved equally unrefreshed, so this is a campaign-wide convention rather than a defect unique to this unit.
findings.why: Non-substantive: the stale resolved-file solver answers are B/C/A/D/B, identical to the post-rename entityfix answers, so no gate outcome is misstated by the omission. Recorded so the 'last records' claim is not read as unqualified.

findings.claim: The post-rename regate turned G-DISTRACTOR q:5 from pass to flag (major), but the unit's final_verify roll-up still records the pre-rename state 'gdistr_flags=0 ... VERIFIED' and was never re-dated, so the shipped summary understates the unit's current gate state.
findings.evidence: verdicts-vfinal/verdicts-gdistractor.jsonl line 25: {"candidate_id": "elf-b8-002", ... "target": "q:5", "verdict": "flag", "findings": [{"severity": "major", "quote": "collapsed", ...}], "executed_by": "claude-opus-4-8/G-DISTRACTOR-entityfix"} - versus the pre-rename line 10 for the same target, which is "verdict":"pass". reviews/final_verify.jsonl line 2 still reads 'gkey_flags=0 gdistr_kills=0 gdistr_flags=0 audit=CONFIRMED audit_major=0 audit_minor=0', date 2026-07-24. By contrast the sibling repair re-dated its roll-up: batch14/reviews/final_verify.jsonl las-b14-001 carries date 2026-07-30.
findings.why: Bookkeeping, and recomputable by re-running vfinal_fold.py - not a correctness defect. The flag itself is disclosed inside the regate record and is self-described there as 'Pre-existing and rename-independent - the entity repair touched only names in the passage', which this audit confirms: the q5 option set is byte-identical to the pre-rename set. Key B remains defensible and both post-rename G-KEY solver votes returned B.

findings.claim: Under a strict reading of 'zero surviving pre-rename names in generator_meta', the unit fails: Bellwether, Ahlgren, Marguerite and Lowe all still appear inside generator_meta.originality_note.
findings.evidence: Field-level walk of candidates-final/elf-b8-002.json reports old-name hits at exactly one path, .generator_meta.originality_note (Bellwether x5, Ahlgren, Marguerite Lowe x2). Passage, title, byline, every prompt, every option, every rationale, generator_meta.fictional_source.byline and generator_meta.fictional_entities[] are clean.
findings.why: Not a defect. Those occurrences are the repair's own provenance record naming what was removed and why; erasing them would destroy the audit trail that makes the repair reviewable. Flagged only so a future automated 'zero survivors' grep over generator_meta is not misread as a regression.

findings.claim: The q5 rationale overstates its case against distractor A: 'assumptions do not "quietly collapse"' asserts a collocational impossibility that is not true of English - 'quietly collapsed' is idiomatic for a failure without fanfare.
findings.evidence: candidates-final/elf-b8-002.json q5 rationale: "collapsed = sense/collocation misfit ('collapse' names a sudden, dramatic failure, which jars against 'quietly'; assumptions do not 'quietly collapse')". The G-DISTRACTOR-entityfix record on the same target reaches the same conclusion independently, calling A 'ARGUABLE' but 'Beatable'.
findings.why: Informational only. The key is still uniquely best: the passage's own evidence is a decade-long drift ('across a decade the share ... has roughly halved'), which selects 'lapsed' (gradual falling out of force) over 'collapsed' (sudden). The defect is that the rationale's teaching payload rests on a false absolute rather than on the gradual-vs-sudden contrast that actually decides the item. Pre-existing: the option text is byte-identical to the pre-rename version, so the rename neither caused nor could fix this.
